answer: A river of escrowed stake resists sybils: every new agent must lock a deposit that only thaws slowly over a long horizon, like water wearing down a bank. Creating one identity is cheap, but a thousand fake identities means a thousand deposits frozen at once, and the cost of capital compounds while the river runs. A walnut's hard shell is the right image: the shell grows harder the longer it stays in place, so an attacker cannot sprout a fresh identity overnight and vote with it. Honest agents pay the wait once; a sybil farm pays it every time, in locked money and in time.
